title: ASKING GOD TO BLESS HIS PEOPLE

memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "Look down from heaven, your holy dwelling place, and bless your people Israel and the land you have given us as you promised on oath to our ancestors, a land flowing with milk and honey." — Deut 26:15 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
The worshipper's declaration ends with a prayer. Having obeyed, he now asks God to look down and bless His people and the land. Notice the ground of his request: "as you promised on oath to our ancestors." He does not ask God to bless them because they deserve it. He appeals to God's own promise, God's own faithfulness.

This is how confident prayer works. We do not come to God pointing to our worthiness; we come pointing to His promises. The Israelite's boldness rested on the sworn word of God, not on his own goodness. God had bound Himself by oath, and He would keep it.

This was a specific prayer for a specific nation and land, so we should not simply claim "milk and honey" prosperity for ourselves. But the way this man prayed teaches us so much. When we pray, we too can appeal to God's promises — and we have even greater ones, guaranteed in Christ. Every promise of God is "Yes" in Him (2 Cor 1:20).

So pray boldly. Ask God to bless, to provide, to work. Not because you have earned His attention, but because He is a promise-keeping God who delights to hear His children and who has already given us His best in His Son.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. When I pray, do I lean on my worthiness or on God's promises?
2. What promise of God can I hold onto in prayer today?
3. How does God's faithfulness give me confidence to ask boldly?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Faithful God, You always keep Your word. I come to You not on my own merit but resting on Your promises in Christ. Look upon Your people and bless us according to Your faithfulness. Amen.
